title: Development and Validation of a Radiologic Immune Quantification System
summary: This study analyzes CT and MRI scans as well as blood samples from patients. The aim is to develop new methods to better assess a person's health and immune strength. Individuals undergoing a CT or MRI scan can participate. The study investigates whether certain features in body images are linked to the immune system and overall health.
conditions: Immune competence as well as disease progression, treatment response, and complications in patients with various diseases, particularly in oncology and cardiology, but not limited to these.

interventions.name:
Observational Study:
Arm 1:
Analysis of CT/MRI imaging and routine clinical data (body structures/ organs, body composition, diagnoses, laboratory values, clinical outcomes) without any additional intervention.

Observational Study:
Arm 2:
Inclusion of patients undergoing CT/MRI imaging, with a blood draw performed prior to the CT/MRI examination, followed by laboratory analyses for the biological validation of radiological biomarkers.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Presence of a clinically indicated CT or MRI examination including imaging of the thorax and/or abdomen or a cardiac CT. For the prospective validation arm additionally: existing venous access and capacity to provide informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Objection to the use of clinical routine data, missing or incomplete imaging data. For the prospective validation arm additionally: lack of capacity to provide informed consent, no venous access.
